beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “A queue-driven worker: one short job per model call, four in flight, one concise sentence back.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the boot beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: an agent and a queue

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Two lines: what it's called, and the queue-worker spine to compile.”

beats.label: Add the agent
beats.cue: The same chat-loop agent the cli target uses — each job's text becomes one single-turn call.

beats.label: Wire the queue
beats.cue: In-memory adapter — no broker to run. The visibility timeout and retry budget live here.

beats.label: Seed eight jobs
beats.cue: seedJobs is the in-memory way to exercise a worker without standing up a real queue.

beats.label: Bound the throughput and the dedup window
beats.cue: “Four jobs in flight per worker process. The 60 seconds is the result cache's TTL, keyed on job id + attempt — the double-pull guard, so two consumers on one lease call the model once.”

beats.label: Scope the permissions
beats.cue: Permissions are a spec block, not a target feature — batch scopes exactly the way cli does.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar — this JSON is what the compiler sees: the agent, the queue, the knobs.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target batch (in-memory queue, 8 seeded jobs)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots the worker: GREEN, with no key.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot ok (booted and exited cleanly)

beats.label: Open the emitted worker
beats.cue: “One file you own: the queue, the consumer, the idempotency store, the drain path.”

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A worker isn't a chat — every other shape ships as a bundle.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "batch")`

beats.label: Boot the worker
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Eight jobs, four in flight — job_start/job_end pairs, then queue_idle, then it stops.”

verify.note: consumes the 8 seeded jobs against Anthropic; deps were installed by the --check beat. Expect fromCache:false on all eight — the key is (job id, attempt), the in-memory adapter bumps attempt on every pull, and ack deletes the job, so nothing in a single-process take can hit the cache.

beats.label: Read one job's transcript
beats.cue: [needs-key] The event stream carries ids and status, never the reply. The session log has both: the job in, the one sentence out.

verify.note: each job is its own runChatLoop, so the worker leaves 8 sessions in .crewhaus/sessions/ (gitignored); with no id, tail picks the most-recently-updated one and dumps `user> …` / `asst> …`. Needs the beat above to have run — the store does not exist otherwise.

groups.title: One more thing · the ops contract you didn't write

beats.label: Find the machinery you never typed
beats.cue: “A keyed dedup cache, a drain path, a SIGTERM handler — emitted from twenty-five lines of YAML.”

verify.note: 12 matching lines in the emitted worker

beats.label: Interrupt it mid-wave
beats.cue: [manual] Boot it again and press ⌃C while jobs are in flight — drain_start, then worker_stop.

verify.note: needs a human at the keyboard to send SIGINT mid-flight (and a key for the jobs to run)
